rule: Representative independence of coset multiplication using normality

conditions.condition: For left cosets, aN=a'N and bN=b'N imply a^{-1}a' and b^{-1}b' lie in N.
conditions.justification: This is the standard equality criterion for left cosets of a subgroup.

conditions.condition: Normality implies b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b belongs to N.
conditions.justification: A normal subgroup is closed under conjugation by every element of G.

conditions.condition: The product b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b(b^{-1}b') lies in N and equals (ab)^{-1}(a'b').
conditions.justification: Subgroup closure gives membership of the product, while cancellation in G gives b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b(b^{-1}b')=b^{-1}a^{-1}a'b'=(ab)^{-1}(a'b').

circularity.justification: The argument proves independence from representatives directly from normality and group algebra, without assuming that the quotient operation is already well-defined.

conclusion.statement: Suppose aN = a'N and bN = b'N. Then a^{-1}a' and b^{-1}b' lie in N. Since N is normal, b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b lies in N; multiplying it by b^{-1}b' shows that (ab)^{-1}(a'b') = b^{-1}(a^{-1}a')b(b^{-1}b') lies in N. Hence abN = a'b'N, so coset multiplication is well-defined.
conclusion.justification: The displayed calculation proves that equal representative choices produce equal product cosets, exactly the required well-definedness condition.
